output:
Dear friends, neighbours, Little Acorns families, and everyone who has checked in or offered to help,

First, I’m safe. I’m staying with my sister in Rondebosch, and Marmalade is safe too. I know some of you have been waiting for a reply since Saturday night. I’m sorry if you’ve been worried. My phone hasn’t stopped, and although I’m so grateful for every message, I just don’t have the energy to answer everyone separately right now.

I’m writing this so there’s one update people can pass on. Please feel free to share it, especially with anyone who is asking how to help or has been sent a fundraiser in my name.

**What happened**

At around 11:40pm on Saturday, 7 November, a fire started in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court on Station Road in Observatory. My flat, number 12, is on the second floor. There are 14 flats in the block, and everyone got out. Two people were treated for smoke inhalation at Groote Schuur and have both been sent home.

The fire department has said it may have been an electrical fault, but they’re still investigating. I don’t want to guess or pass on anything that hasn’t been confirmed.

Our neighbour, Uncle Faizel, banged on every door on our floor in his vest and slippers. That’s how I woke up. I grabbed my phone and Marmalade and got out with nothing else. Marmalade then hid under a car for two hours, which was quite enough extra terror for one night, but he’s with me now.

My flat has extensive smoke and water damage, and the ceiling came down in the lounge. The landlord has said nobody can move back in for at least six weeks. I don’t yet know what, if anything, I’ll be able to save.

That’s about as much of the story as I can tell at the moment. Please understand if I don’t want to go through the whole night again. I’m exhausted, and I’m still trying to take in what has happened.

**Thank you**

People have been so kind. I’ve been crying at just about every message, including the ones I haven’t managed to answer.

One of my school moms left a bag of clothes at my sister’s gate at 7am on Sunday. She didn’t even knock. She just made sure I had something to wear. That sort of practical, quiet kindness has meant so much.

And Uncle Faizel: thank you. I don’t really have words big enough for what it means that you went from door to door making sure we were awake.

I keep reminding myself that furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can’t. Neither can any of the people in our building. I’m devastated about my home, and I’m also so grateful that everyone got out.

**What would help right now**

I hate asking for help. I feel awkward even writing this part, but lots of people have asked what I actually need, and it makes more sense to be specific.

The things that would help most are:

- **Help towards a deposit for a new place.** Finding somewhere to live is the biggest practical worry at the moment.
- **Shoes for school/work, size 6, and work clothes, size 34.** I have enough general clothing now, but I still need suitable things to teach in.
- **A working laptop.** If anyone has an older laptop they no longer use, it would make an enormous difference. It doesn’t need to be new or fancy. All my lesson planning was on mine.

If you have one of those specific things to offer, please leave a comment or send me a message saying what it is. I’ll get back to you as I can, though it might take a little while.

**What I don’t need**

Thank you so much to everyone who has sent clothes and food. For now, I don’t need any more general clothing, apart from the work things mentioned above. I already have more than I can use, and I’ll pass the extras on to people from the other flats.

My sister’s freezer is also full, so we’re sorted for food. Please don’t feel you need to send a meal or buy groceries. You’ve already helped us so much in that department.

**The fundraiser — and an important warning**

My friend Zinhle has set up a BackaBuddy fundraiser for me:

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**

The target is **R25 000**, and as of this morning, it had reached **R11 400**. I’m honestly overwhelmed by that. I felt very strange about having a fundraiser, but Zinhle told me to shut up and accept the help, so I’m trying.

If you’ve donated or shared the page, thank you. Please don’t feel any pressure to contribute if you’re not in a position to. Checking in and being patient with me matters too.

**There is also an unrelated “Thandi Fire Relief” page being circulated, along with a WhatsApp message asking people to EFT money into a Capitec account. Neither is mine or connected to our fundraiser. Please do not send money to them. I’ve reported it.**

The BackaBuddy link above is the only fundraiser Zinhle has set up for me. If someone forwards you another appeal in my name, please send them this letter so they have the correct information.

**For my Little Acorns families**

To the parents of my Ladybirds at Little Acorns Pre-Primary: the concert on **27 November is still happening**. Please don’t worry.

The 22 crowns and the children’s handprint banner that I brought home to laminate were lost in the fire. That has been a particularly sore thing to think about. But the Ladybirds will have crowns. We’ll make a plan.

I’m back at school on Wednesday. Please don’t make a big thing of my return in front of the children. I know any fuss would come from love, but I’d really appreciate being able to get back into our usual school day without having to talk about the fire in front of them.

Finally, please don’t take a slow reply, or an unanswered DM, as a sign that your message hasn’t mattered. I’m reading what I can and answering slowly. Sometimes I just don’t know what to say beyond thank you.

Thank you for helping me, for caring about Marmalade, and for giving me some room to catch my breath.

With love,  
Thandi
